basics.name: Juyi Lin
basics.label: PhD Student in Computer Engineering
basics.summary: PhD student at Northeastern University working on generative world models, video reasoning benchmarks, and efficient Vision-Language-Action models. Advisor: Prof. Yanzhi Wang.

education.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

work.name: Futurewei Technologies, Inc.
work.summary: Research Intern, Generative AI & World Modeling team.
highlights: Built LEAP, a coarse-to-fine perception router on top of Qwen3 30BA3B omni model, improving the watch-the-whole-clip baseline by +6.0 pt on OmniVideoBench, and staying +3 pt overall across 5 public long-video QA benchmarks.

work.name: Beijing VirtAI Tech
highlights: Integrated PaddlePaddle distribution library and Deep Graph Library (DGL) into the performance measurement system.
Conducted an in-depth performance analysis of PaddlePaddle distributed training.

projects.name: Physical Reasoning Benchmark for Generative World Models
highlights: Proposed and built PhyGround, a criteria-grounded benchmark for physical reasoning in generative video world models across a taxonomy of 13 physical laws (solid-body mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics), evaluating 8 video models.
Led a large-scale human annotation study involving 459 annotators, 5,796 complete annotations, 37.4K+ fine-grained labels, with split-half ranking correlation Spearman's ρ > 0.90.
Trained and released PhyJudge-9B, an open physics-specialized VLM judge that achieves 3.3% aggregate relative bias vs. 16.6% for Gemini-3.1-Pro.

projects.name: Video Reasoning Benchmark
highlights: Proposed and implemented VBVR-EvalKit, a benchmark for evaluating reasoning capabilities in video generation models, covering 40 models.

Co-lead a team of 22 researchers, designing the data generation and benchmark framework, defining the development roadmap, and contributing core code and evaluation metrics. Launched an open-source ecosystem including 100+ synthetic data generators.
Proposed and built a video reasoning dataset, covering 200 curated reasoning tasks and 1M+ video clips (1000× larger than prior datasets).

projects.name: Vision Language Action (VLA) Model
projects.summary: NEU & Funded by EmbodyX, Jan 2025 – Sept 2025
highlights: Proposed VOTE, an efficient fine-tuning framework for parallel action prediction in VLA models, reducing computational overhead and accelerating inference. Used by Cisco and EmbodyX.
Proposed an ensemble voting strategy for the action sampling, improving model performance and enhancing generalization across diverse tasks.

Improved the average success rates of OpenVLA by over 20% across four LIBERO task suites, surpassed 7% average success rate of the state-of-the-art VLA model in SimplerEnv WidowX Robot, and accelerated action generation throughput by 39× on edge device NVIDIA Jetson Orin.
Pretrained Llama3.2-1B LLM into a vision-language model (VLM) and fine-tuned with VOTE method, surpassing 7B OpenVLA's average success rate by 16% across four LIBERO task suites.
